sources.entry: django - A high-level web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

summary.one_liner: Django is a high-level Python web framework built for rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a short orientation page rather than a full feature list. It points readers to the docs directory for installation instructions, a tutorial series, deployment guidance, topical guides, HOWTOs, and the reference. It also describes how to build an HTML copy of the docs and how to run Django's test suite via the contributing guide. It links to a ticket tracker for reporting docs problems, plus a Discord community and a Django Forum for help. Contribution guidance and a section asking readers to support the Django Software Foundation are included.
use_cases: setting up a Python web project quickly
learning web development with a structured tutorial
deploying a Python website to a server
contributing to an open-source web framework
how_to_run: Work through docs/intro/tutorial01.txt onward in order
Follow docs/howto/deployment/index.txt to set up a deployment server
See docs/README to build an HTML version of the docs
Follow the Unit tests section in docs/internals/contributing/writing-code/unit-tests.txt to run the test suite
notable: Documentation lives in the repo's docs directory with a guided reading order
Includes a built-in path from installation through tutorials to deployment
Community support via a Discord server and an official forum
Public ticket system where users can report documentation problems
caveats: The README does not list features or code examples; details are in the external docs
The README does not state a license
